newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chun Tai seen strong on debut - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Chun Tai seen strong on debut - analysts.

text.p: Shares of consumer electronics products manufacturer Chun Tai Holdings Ltd are poised for a strong trading debut on Monday due to their high subscription rate and grey market price, analysts said on Friday.
"A strong debut is expected due to its warm flotation response and in view of its grey market price," said Michael Ng, analyst at ASG Investment.
Analysts said the grey market price was about HK$1.50 per share compared with an issue price of HK$1.03.
Chun Tai offered 82 million new shares at HK$1.03 each in an initial public offer. The 73.80 million shares available to the general public were 168.41 times subscribed.
"However, short-term speculators are likely to take profit on the first day of trading and that may cap its rise in the short run," said a research manager at a local brokerage.
Analysts said they were cautiously optimistic on the company's earnings prospects due to its relationship with existing customers and the growth potential of video compact disc (VCD) products.
But the company's reliance on only a few customers was a risk factor that must be considered, analysts said.

Chun Tai said in its listing prospectus that sales of audio products for Casio Computer Co Ltd and a range of toys based on cartoon characters for Mattel Inc accounted for about 30 percent and 39 percent respectively of turnover for the year ended March 31, 1996.
The company said net proceeds from the flotation of about HK$71 million would be used to establish a new plant in China, finance research and development and repay bank borrowings.
